Even taking the driver's contact attempts at face value, they do not make the fee chargeable: 2 in-app messages and 1 unanswered call (F6, F11, F12, F14) satisfy NS-1(iii), but a satisfied contact condition cannot rescue a fee whose waiting-time and presence conditions are the only ones in dispute, and the fee must be voided if any NS-1 condition fails (NS-2).

The 3 min 20 s GPS gap between 14:09:10 and 14:12:30 (F1) leaves the driver's continuous presence unproven for the middle of the wait, which under NS-1(iv) and TH-4 cannot be used against the rider — a gap in the records favours neither party, so the unproven stretch cannot be counted as chargeable waiting time in the driver's favour.

The rider's complaint that she came down a minute after the cancellation is consistent with the record: the cancellation was at 14:13:40 and the fee of $5.00 was charged on that cancellation (F5, F9); she had a 1.0x, no-surge trip (F10) and an 1165-day account with 0 upheld disputes and 0 prior no-shows in 90 days (F19), so there is no pattern of no-shows justifying the charge.

The dispute is a $5.00 fixed-fee no-show/cancellation matter, final at system level (TH-2), and the outcome sought is refund_full of $5.00 as computed from the cancellation fee on record (F9), not a routing or surge issue (no off-route segment; F10 shows 1.0x surge).

The GPS gap 14:09:10-14:12:30 (F1) cuts both ways under TH-4: because it favours neither party, the judge may treat the middle of the wait as undecided rather than as proof for the rider, and the driver's stationary position at 40 m (F4) is the only continuous-presence evidence before and after the gap.

claims.assertion: The driver arrived and was physically at the pickup point: he tapped "I'm Here" at 14:07:40 only 40 m from the pickup (F8), his closest approach was 26 m at 14:07:35 (F2), and the platform recorded arrival at 14:07:40 (F7). That satisfies NS-1(i).

That satisfies NS-1(iii).

All four NS-1 conditions hold on the system records, so the $5.00 no-show fee stands and is payable to the driver; NS-2 voiding is not triggered (no condition failed, and GPS placed him at the pickup, not away from it).

The cancellation was recorded against reason rider_no_show, and the app record of who cancelled and why is the system record of the ground for cancellation (F5); the driver's post-trip statement (F15) is consistent with that record, so this is an NS-1/NS-2 case, not an NS-3 "driver cancelled for another reason" case.

The rider's "I got downstairs a minute after he cancelled" is a statement after the fact (complaint) and is contradicted by the system records: the driver was within 200 m from 14:07:15, waited 6 min after arrival and 8 min 40 s after acceptance, and had by then messaged twice and called once (F3, F4, F6, F7).

The fare record shows the fee charged was exactly $5.00 with a 1.0x multiplier, i.e. the standard NS-1 cancellation fee and nothing more (F9, F10), so there is no overcharge to refund under RD-2 or otherwise.

No traffic, weather or safety issue affects this case: no incidents near the route (F17), fair weather (F18), and nothing in the chat, complaint or statement alleges threats, harassment or dangerous driving (F11, F12, F14, F15), so SAFE-1 escalation is not engaged.
The $5.00 no-show charge is a fixed-sum category that is system-final under TH-2 and TH-1 (under $10), so no human review is required for this dispute type.

points.response: I do not contest that the arrival element is met: the tap at 14:07:40 with GPS 40 m from the pickup (F8, F7) satisfies NS-1(i), and my brief has always measured the wait from that tap.

The presence condition is not cleanly met: the GPS trace has no samples at all between 14:09:10 and 14:12:30 (F1), so the middle 3 min 20 s of the claimed 6 min 0 s stationary period (F4) is exactly the stretch NS-1(iv) requires to be proven, and TH-4 says a gap favours neither party rather than the driver.

The arithmetic cuts against the driver, not for him: cancellation at 14:13:40 is 6 min 0 s after his own arrival tap at 14:07:40 (F7, F8) — under NS-1(ii) the 5-minute free wait counted from the later of scheduled pickup and arrival leaves well under a minute of chargeable waiting when he cancelled — and the DISP-002 8-minute threshold he invokes runs from arrival, not acceptance, so his 8 min 40 s from acceptance (F5) does not reach it.

NS-1(iii) is met as to form — 2 in-app messages with the first at 14:08:10 (F6, F11) and 1 in-app call at 14:09 (F6, F14) — but the call was not answered and has no recording (F14); contact conditions that are satisfied cannot cure a fee whose waiting-time condition is the failing element, since NS-2 voids the fee if any condition fails.

NS-2 is triggered by a single failed condition, and here the wait was not competently exceeded (F7, F8) and continuous presence across the 14:09:10–14:12:30 gap is unproven (F1), so at least one NS-1 condition fails and the $5.00 must be refunded in full.

The driver's own message at 14:13 reads as a timing claim — "More than 5 min already, I have to cancel" (F12) — which on the record clock (arrival tap 14:07:40, cancel 14:13:40; F7, F8) was simply untrue, so the app's rider_no_show label does not convert a premature cancellation into a valid NS-1 no-show.

The rider's complaint is not contradicted by any system record on the point that matters: she was not required to appear before the free wait from the later of scheduled pickup and arrival had run, and the system record shows the driver cancelled before that grace could fairly elapse on the post-gap evidence (F1, F7, F8).

The amount is not in dispute — $5.00 at 1.0x surge (F9, F10) — what is in dispute is whether the fee was chargeable at all, and under NS-2 an unchargeable fee is refunded in full regardless of it being the standard figure.

Agreed: nothing in the chat, call log or complaint alleges threats, harassment or dangerous driving (F11, F12, F14), so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is not engaged and this stays a fixed-fee no-show matter.

System-finality is about the path, not the outcome: TH-2 makes the no-show category system-final, and TH-1 governs amounts under $10, both of which are satisfied by refunding the $5.00 cancellation fee on record (F9) under NS-2 rather than escalating.

As add-on support for our side rather than a contest of theirs: the rider has a 1165-day account, rating 4.5, and 0 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F19), while the driver already carries 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 days (F20); the profile is offered only as credibility support and never decides the case.

The rider misreads NS-1(ii): the free wait runs 5 minutes from the LATER of scheduled pickup time and arrival — here arrival at 14:07:40 (F7, F8) — so it expired at 14:12:40, and the driver cancelled at 14:13:40, a full 6 min 0 s later (F4, F7). On no reading is "More than 5 min already" (F12) premature; and even if it were, DISP-002's 8-minute record threshold (8 min 40 s from acceptance, F5) is met.

The rider's own timeline confirms every NS-1 limb: arrival tap at 40 m with GPS at the pickup (F7, F8, F2), stationary 40 m from pickup through cancellation (F4), and cancellation 6 min 0 s after arrival and 8 min 40 s after acceptance (F5, F7). Those are the chargeable conditions met, not merely the two the rider concedes.

The waiting-time and presence conditions are not merely satisfied but satisfied by the rider's own admitted facts (F4, F7, F8), so there is no failed NS-1 condition for NS-2 to operate on; the contact condition (F6, F11, F14) is a fourth limb that also holds, making all four met.

The 3 min 20 s GPS gap (F1) is bridged by record evidence on both sides of it: the platform recorded a single stationary period 14:07:40–14:13:40 at 40 m from the pickup (F4), the arrival tap and a 6 min 0 s stay inside 200 m (F7, F8), and 6 min 25 s cumulative time within 200 m (F3). TH-4 escalation is for a condition left undecidable, and presence here is decided by F4/F7/F8, so the gap is not outcome-relevant and nothing needs to be escalated.

The rider's profile (F19) proves no prior no-show pattern, and we do not rely on one: the fee stands on the single trip's records (F4, F7, F8, F6), not on any history. The 1.0x multiplier (F10) is likewise irrelevant — the $5.00 cancellation fee is flat and not surged (F9).

We agree the dispute is system-final under TH-2 and that the fee on record is $5.00 (F9, F5); the disagreement is only whether it is voidable, and all four NS-1 conditions are met, so NS-2's refund_full does not apply and the fee stands.

I withdraw the part of D3 that leans on DISP-002's 8-minute threshold as a record threshold for this trip: no such threshold appears in this record, so the correct reading is the policy default — 5 minutes from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival, expired at 14:12:40 against a 14:13:40 cancellation (F5, F7).
